data.title: 4Mobility Issues Second Notice on Planned Corporate Division by Separation
data.description:
4Mobility S.A. ( (PL:4MB) ) just unveiled an announcement.

4Mobility S.A. has issued a second formal notice to shareholders of its plan to divide the company by separation under the Polish Commercial Companies Code, transferring part of its assets to subsidiary 4Mobility Rent sp. z o.o. The move is structured as a division by separation, with the subsidiary designated as the acquiring company, signaling a planned reorganization of the group’s operational and asset structure.

The division plan and supporting financial and management documents for the last three years have been made freely available on the company’s website and will remain accessible until shareholder meetings conclude. This disclosure supports informed voting on the division resolutions and indicates a significant corporate restructuring that may reshape 4Mobility’s governance and asset allocation, with direct implications for current shareholders.

data.description:

On September 11, 2026, Jaguar Health exchanged a 6% convertible promissory note held by Lincoln Alternative Strategies for 557,377 shares of common stock, cancelling the $175,016.36 note balance and further shifting its liabilities into equity. Between July 7 and September 14, 2026, the company also retired 9.2 shares of its Series Q Preferred Stock held by Streeterville Capital through three privately negotiated exchanges, issuing a total of 304,473 common shares, a dilution exceeding 5% of shares outstanding as of August 19, 2026.

On September 12, 2026, Jaguar Health agreed to issue 535,000 common shares and a pre-funded warrant for 2,077,255 shares to a minority shareholder of Napo Therapeutics, and the purchase transaction closed on September 15, 2026. This deal consolidated full ownership of Napo Therapeutics under Jaguar’s corporate group while relying on private offering exemptions, and collectively the transactions reduced preferred and debt obligations at the cost of increased common equity dilution for existing shareholders.
